title: neptune-fork: rebuilding Le Verrier's 1846 Neptune prediction as a Bayesian inference
description: neptune-fork rebuilds Le Verrier's 1846 prediction of Neptune from Uranus's observed motion, from first principles: its own Wisdom–Holman symplectic N-body integrator (validated against REBOUND), a forward model that fits Uranus's orbit jointly with an unseen perturber, and partitioned nested sampling (dynesty) for multimodal posteriors and Bayesian evidence, checked by coverage tests on synthetic data. It fits the 279 observations of Le Verrier's own 1846 Table 77 with an apparent-place observation model and per-observer error calibration. The pre-registered fit puts the unseen planet at 325.8° on the night Galle found Neptune, with a 68 % interval of 323.6°–327.8°, against Neptune's true 325.87°. The transcribed Table 77 is published as a separate dataset (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24044791).
